findings.issue: The Vitest day-boundary assertions (AC#3, SPEC-11 localDay cases) build times with local-time constructors in whatever TZ the process has. On a UTC runner (CI is ubuntu-24.04, no TZ set) local == UTC, so a mutation that keys days by UTC date (e.g. completedAt.slice(0,10)) passes every Vitest test. Only the e2e spec (timezoneId America/New_York) catches it.
findings.evidence: All 17 new Vitest tests pass under TZ=UTC, TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati and TZ=America/Los_Angeles; under TZ=UTC localDay and a UTC-slice implementation are indistinguishable. The e2e spec does catch it: a UTC key would put the 23:58 New York session wholly on 11 Nov and give 2 per-day 6-max points instead of 3.
findings.fix: Optional: pin a non-UTC zone for the grouping tests, e.g. set process.env.TZ = 'America/New_York' in a Vitest setup or test env, or add one unit case that builds a UTC ISO time whose local date differs in a fixed zone. Not required, because the e2e spec already guards this in CI.

findings.issue: Under Session/Day, sessionStartTimes(data) is built twice: once inside orderHands and again for groupHands. Under Day the second one is not used at all.
findings.evidence: const groups = hands === 0 ? [] : groupHands(order(), grouping, sessionStartTimes(data));
findings.fix: Optional: pass the start function only for 'session', or leave it as is. It is linear and cheap.

findings.issue: perPoint, chartNote and bb100Note insert the TrendGrouping id ('session'/'day') straight into user-visible text, so the ids also act as copy.
findings.fix: Optional: leave it. The unit tests pin every resulting string, so a rename would be caught.

summary: The change matches the spec. Default grouping takes the unchanged per-500 code path and its points have no group key (pinned by Object.keys). Session grouping reuses orderHands. sessionStartTimes is factored out and not duplicated, so start order, the earliest-completedAt fallback and the sessionId tie-break all match. Day grouping keys each hand by the local date of its own completedAt, so a session past midnight splits across days, and the buckets are sorted. Calendar-day keys are safe across DST changes. BB/100 skips groups with no cash hands and shares the group object with the Major point. App resets grouping on every opening and on load, keeps it on filter changes, keeps the filter on grouping changes, and ignores changes while data is undefined. G-2 still comes from all stored hands. Tests use reversed or shuffled input. nineSessions has start order different from id order, which catches ordering sessions by id. The 119/281 counts catch day-by-session-start. AC#8 compares against real sessionReport values. The e2e spec passes in Chromium and WebKit, and its New York zone catches a UTC-day mutation. Vitest alone would not on a UTC runner (MINOR). Minus sign: ASCII '-' is correct. signedTenths prints '-', and TASK-11.2 / session-report tests and the docs already use it. The spec's §5 table showing U+2212 is a typo. Scope 982 vs 760 lines: about 290 source, 650 tests and 41 docs. The tests cover 12 behaviour items, including a 3,000-hand recompute and real played sessions, so the overrun is justified. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
